translationRepairs: Then Yue explained: "In all the realm only literary craft, the Changes, and chess matter—and you walk off with every one at once; that is stinginess indeed."
Then Yue explained: "In all the realm only literary arts, chess, and calligraphy matter—and you walk off with every one at once; that is stinginess indeed."
文義棋書 is literary arts, chess, and calligraphy (書), not the Changes (易); the proposal rightly drops 易 but wrongly turns 不廉 into "greed"—s0008's tease already renders 不廉 as stinginess/ungenerous.
Yue then said: "Under heaven there are only literary arts, the Changes, and chess—yet you carry them all off at once; one might call that ungenerous indeed."
Yue then said: "Under heaven there are only literary arts, chess, and calligraphy—yet you carry them all off at once; one might call that ungenerous indeed."
書 in 文義棋書 is calligraphy/writing, not the Changes; keep 不廉 as ungenerous (matching s0008), not "greedy."

司徒掾 is clerk to the Situ (Minister over the Masses); "clerk in the Secretariat" invents a 尚書 office not in the Chinese.

Chinese has 叔齊, not 伯夷; the literal must read Shu Qi.
